plan.notes: Transcribed from the official SCC 'Enhanced Air Traffic Control Certificate' program map, Catalog 2026-27, published May 10, 2026 (mapmaker.losrios.edu/Maps/7802/PublishedPdf). Official Total Units: 29; this seed = 1 + 12 + 12 + 4 = 29 units. Semester sums verified against the map's 1 / 12 / 12 / 4 headers. This seed models the Tower Cohort path (first-listed options); the En Route Cohort substitutes ATC 320-323 for 310-313 and ATC 325 for 315. Choice slots: (1) ATC 310 / 320 Enhanced Air Traffic Control Terminal 1/En Route 1 (3) — ATC 310 selected; (2) ATC 311 / 321 (3) — ATC 311 selected; (3) ATC 312 / 322 (3) — ATC 312 selected; (4) ATC 313 / 323 (3) — ATC 313 selected; (5) ATC 315 / 325 Terminal/En Route Simulation Training (4) — ATC 315 selected. In-plan prereqs (Tower path): ATC 300 requires ATC 200; ATC 301 requires ATC 300; ATC 302 requires ATC 301; ATC 303 requires ATC 302; ATC 310 requires ATC 300, 301, 302, and 303; ATC 311 requires ATC 310; ATC 312 requires ATC 311; ATC 313 requires ATC 312; ATC 315 requires ATC 313 — all with grades of 'C' or better. En Route path prereqs documented (not in-plan): ATC 320 requires 300-303; ATC 321 requires 320; ATC 322 requires 321; ATC 323 requires 322; ATC 325 requires 323. PreReq ATC 200 is a program-entry prerequisite, modeled as a major course. Certificate of Achievement requirements: grade of 'C' or better in each major course. Documented enrollment eligibility (FAA): English language proficiency (ICAO Level 4 / AC60-28); under 31 years old by tentative job offer (FAA direct hire; nonFAA contract facilities exempt); minimum one year of general work experience, one year of full-time college, or equivalent combination; Federal Security Clearance background check; Class 3 Airman Medical Exam to enter, FAA-endorsed medical/drug/psychological exams at graduation; qualifying ATSA score before program completion for FAA direct-hire consideration. Air Traffic Control, Business and Industry Meta Majors. tccns mirrors SCC local course codes (California community colleges do not use TCCNS).
